pr.body:
This adds a hook that can be implemented to produce an occurrence specific to the detector that is subclassing the StatefulDetector.

Also change the signature of evaluate to return a dict keyed by groupkey instead of a list. This helps avoid the chance of duplicate results for the same group key.

<!-- Describe your PR here. -->
pr.title: feat(workflow_engine): Add in hook for producing occurrences from the stateful detector

raw_findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data) that MetricAlertDetectorHandler does not implement, so instantiating it raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. The uncaught exception aborts process_detectors for the whole batch, whereas the previous concrete evaluate() returned an empty list safely.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Runtime TypeError when the workflow engine tries to build a handler for any metric_alert_fire detector, crashing detector processing instead of degrading gracefully.
raw_findings.impact: StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data) that MetricAlertDetectorHandler does not implement, so instantiating it raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. The uncaught exception aborts process_detectors for the whole batch, whereas the previous concrete evaluate() returned an empty list safely.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch changed the base class from DetectorHandler with a concrete evaluate() to the abstract StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, while leaving the class registered as a detector_handler.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either implement the abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) with stub bodies on MetricAlertDetectorHandler, or stop assigning it as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler until it is concrete.
raw_findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class but is still wired as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, causing TypeError on instantiation
raw_findings.trigger: A Detector row with type "metric_alert_fire" is passed to process_detectors, which accesses detector.detector_handler and calls group_type.detector_handler(self).

raw_findings.body: IssueOccurrence is a frozen dataclass compared field-by-field, so the fingerprint mismatch makes the equality assertion fail (or, at minimum, the expected value does not describe the behavior the test claims to verify), breaking the new test's ability to validate the occurrence hook output.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The new test asserts against an occurrence whose fingerprint cannot match the one produced by the code under test, causing a deterministic test failure or a misleading assertion.
raw_findings.impact: IssueOccurrence is a frozen dataclass compared field-by-field, so the fingerprint mismatch makes the equality assertion fail (or, at minimum, the expected value does not describe the behavior the test claims to verify), breaking the new test's ability to validate the occurrence hook output.
raw_findings.root_cause: Inconsistent group key literals between the expected-occurrence construction and the actual evaluate_group_key_value invocation in the newly added test assertions.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Build the expected occurrence with the same group key that is passed to evaluate_group_key_value, i.e. build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "group_key", 10, PriorityLevel.HIGH).
raw_findings.title: test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence with group key "val1" while evaluating group key "group_key", producing a fingerprint mismatch
raw_findings.trigger: Running TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe: evaluate_group_key_value is called with expected_result.group_key == "group_key", so the handler builds an occurrence with fingerprint ["{id}:group_key"], while the expected occurrence was built with group_key "val1" giving fingerprint ["{id}:val1"].

raw_findings.body: The docstring now contradicts the return annotation (dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey vs. list), misleading implementers of subclasses and callers about the contract this patch deliberately changed.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale documentation describes the removed list-based contract, degrading review quality and future maintenance of detector handler subclasses.
raw_findings.impact: The docstring now contradicts the return annotation (dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey vs. list), misleading implementers of subclasses and callers about the contract this patch deliberately changed.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch changed evaluate's return type from list to dict but did not update the adjacent docstring describing the return value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the docstring to state that evaluate returns a dict of DetectorEvaluationResult keyed by group key, with one entry per group key in the packet.
raw_findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list after the signature was changed to return a dict
raw_findings.trigger: A developer reads the docstring immediately below the changed signature: "Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`."

raw_findings.body: No test exercises or verifies that the correct group value is forwarded to the new build_occurrence_and_event_data hook; a regression that passes the wrong value (or the wrong group's value) to the hook would not be caught by any of the added tests.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The added hook's `value` argument is effectively untested, weakening coverage of the primary new behavior introduced by this patch.
raw_findings.impact: No test exercises or verifies that the correct group value is forwarded to the new build_occurrence_and_event_data hook; a regression that passes the wrong value (or the wrong group's value) to the hook would not be caught by any of the added tests.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new test helper accepts a `value` parameter but never uses it, allowing call sites with values inconsistent with the evaluated data packet to pass silently.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the actual packet value (10) at this call site and make build_mock_occurrence_and_event incorporate `value` into the produced occurrence (e.g., in evidence_data or subtitle) so equality assertions detect a wrong value being passed to the hook.
